message.content: {"caption":"Two-panel chart comparing short-term learning curves with stacked long-term performance across four Navi settings and a baseline.","description":"The left panel, “Short-term Performance (0–20 steps),” plots Avg@4 (%) against Training Steps at 0, 10, and 20. The dashed gray Baseline rises from about 14.5 to 28.5 to a printed 43.0. Navi (ε̂_high=0.4, orange) rises from about 14.5 to 25.8 to a printed 39.5; Navi (ε̂_high=0.6, blue) from about 15.5 to 32 to a printed 40.8; Navi (ε̂_high=0.8, green) from about 15 to 32 to a printed 44.0; and Navi (ε̂_high=1.0, purple) from about 16.5 to 36.5 to a printed 45.2. All lines increase; the 1.0 setting is highest at step 20, while 0.4 is lowest. The right panel, “Long-term Performance (20–80 steps),” shows stacked bars for Baseline and the four Navi settings, with Avg@4 (%) on a vertical axis beginning at 30. Solid lower sections represent Step 0–20 and hatched upper sections Step 20–80; each pair uses the corresponding gray, orange, blue, green, or purple color. Estimated solid-section top-edge readings are 43.0, 39.5, 40.7, 44.0, and 45.0, respectively. Estimated hatched-section top edges—and thus cumulative bar totals—are 51.3, 57.3, 61.0, 59.8, and 53.0, respectively. The hatched section’s added height is the difference between that cumulative total and the solid-section top edge. Navi 0.6 has the greatest long-term cumulative total; 0.4 and 0.8 are next, while 1.0 is lower than the baseline total. No arrows or check/cross marks are
